concepts.title: Types of Forests in India
concepts.definition: India's natural vegetation ranges from tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in heavy rainfall areas, tropical deciduous or monsoon forests of moist and dry types, tropical thorn forests of arid zones, montane forests by altitude, to littoral and swamp forests of mangroves in deltas.
concepts.key_idea: Tropical deciduous forests are the most widespread, shedding leaves in the dry season, while evergreen forests show multi-storeyed diversity above 200 cm rainfall.

concepts.title: Forest Conservation and Social Forestry
concepts.definition: Forest conservation rests on joint forest management with local communities, social forestry of farm and avenue planting, protection of biodiversity through national parks and sanctuaries, and wildlife protection laws against depletion of forest cover.
concepts.key_idea: The Forest Conservation policy and joint forest management involve villagers in protecting degraded forests, sharing benefits of regeneration.

concepts.title: Forest Cover, Uses and Biodiversity Value
concepts.definition: Forests cover about a fifth of India's area, providing timber, fuel, fodder, bamboo, medicinal plants and habitat for biodiversity, and the National Forest Policy aims at one third of the land under forest to maintain ecological balance.
concepts.key_idea: Forests regulate climate, hold soils against erosion and recharge water, so their conservation serves both economic use and ecological stability.
